report.summary: Chunk 2 of 3: CodexCliProvider class with egress gate, subprocess spawning, and timeout handling.
risks: codex exec subprocess | high | Subprocess may hang if stdin not closed; code closes stdin via subprocess.DEVNULL, but comment notes historical hang. | Verify that subprocess.DEVNULL prevents hang in all environments.
encoding utf-8 errors replace | medium | Using errors='replace' may silently corrupt non-UTF-8 output; comment says codex emits UTF-8. | Test with actual codex output containing non-UTF-8 bytes.
writable flag disk_may_be_dirty | medium | Timeout or non-zero exit sets disk_may_be_dirty=True, but no rollback logic is present in this chunk. | Check if caller handles dirty disk state.

claims.text: Egress-gated exactly like DeepSeek (trusted_with_ip=False): a task with policy-denied paths/content is refused before any subprocess is spawned.
claims.why: No DeepSeek code in this chunk to compare; the egress gate logic is present but the claim of 'exactly like DeepSeek' cannot be verified.
can_write=True is set, and the subcommand includes --sandbox workspace-write when writable is True.

claims.text: external API -- bytes leave the machine

claims.why: trusted_with_ip=False is set, and the run method checks classify_data and returns blocked_report if sensitive.

claims.text: 300s killed C2's wrapper while codex kept working and the report went out as blocked despite good disk changes.
claims.why: References historical measurement and behavior of codex; no code in this chunk to verify the claim.

claims.text: fail-closed: caller must grant write explicitly
claims.why: writable defaults to False, and the subcommand uses --sandbox read-only when writable is False.

claims.text: HARD EGRESS GATE (non-negotiable): same enforcement path as DeepSeek. Refuse BEFORE spawning the CLI -- a denied path never reaches codex.
claims.why: The egress gate logic is present (classify_data check), but the claim of 'same enforcement path as DeepSeek' cannot be verified without DeepSeek code.
The try block writes a file but catches OSError and passes, so it is never fatal.

claims.text: npm installs `codex` as a .CMD shim on Windows; subprocess cannot spawn it by bare name (WinError 2), so resolve the real path.
claims.why: Code uses shutil.which('codex') to resolve the path, which handles .CMD shims on Windows.

claims.text: codex emits UTF-8 (em-dashes, box-drawing chars); WITHOUT an explicit encoding, text=True decodes with the Windows locale (cp1252) and the capture reader-thread dies on bytes like 0x9d -> corrupted/empty output, watcher thread crash (live-fired 2026-07-12, tasks C2/C3). Force UTF-8 and never let a stray byte kill the reader.
claims.why: Code sets encoding='utf-8' and errors='replace' in subprocess.run.

claims.text: stdin MUST be closed: with a prompt arg, `codex exec` still appends piped/inherited stdin as a <stdin> block and blocks until EOF. Under the file-bridge watcher the inherited stdin never closes -> codex hangs at ~0 CPU (live-fired 2026-07-11, task C1).

claims.why: The message is constructed with the timeout_s parameter.

observations.what: The class docstring claims egress-gating is exactly like DeepSeek, but no DeepSeek code is present to compare.
The timeout_s docstring references historical measurements and behavior, but no evidence is in this chunk.
The subprocess error handling for non-zero exit code is incomplete; the chunk ends mid-statement.
The code writes a debug file to RUN_DIR/last_codex_prompt.md but silently ignores OSError; this could hide configuration issues.
